name: Gou Ji (Gao Ji)
description: Gou Ji (often transliterated as Gao Ji) is a massive, chaotic, and highly strategic climbing card game from Shandong Province, China. It is famous for using four full decks of cards mixed together (216 cards total) and is played by six players divided into two teams of three. The name 'Gou Ji' means 'Enough Level' or 'Sufficient Rank', referring to the special high-ranking combinations that trigger 'Duels' between opposing players. It is a game of chaotic bursts of action, intricate teamwork, and psychological warfare.

content.text: Gou Ji (often transliterated as Gao Ji) is a massive, chaotic, and highly strategic climbing card game from Shandong Province, China. It is famous for using four full decks of cards mixed together (216 cards total) and is played by six players divided into two teams of three. The name 'Gou Ji' means 'Enough Level' or 'Sufficient Rank', referring to the special high-ranking combinations that trigger 'Duels' between opposing players. It is a game of chaotic bursts of action, intricate teamwork, and psychological warfare.
Originating in Qingdao, Shandong in the 1960s, Gou Ji became a cultural phenomenon in Northern China. It was developed to accommodate large groups of players with a surplus of cards.
6 players. Seated alternating (Team A: 1, 3, 5; Team B: 2, 4, 6).
4 decks of 52 cards + 8 Jokers (4 Red, 4 Black). Total 216 cards.
